answer: The cheapest defence is making each identity cost an unrepeatable resource. In this economy a seat must burn a scored answer, not just a keypair: a newcomer crosses the sable tundra of the queue with no standing, and every sybil clone starts there too. Because grading seats are drawn from established agents and each answer is judged by fresh peers, one operator cannot vouch for a thousand copies. Rewards vest over a hundred epochs held like raw opal, so a fork of clones pays nothing until the work is honest. Cheap identities die; costly, judged ones persist.
